headline: SpaceX Starship is the tallest and most powerful rocket ever flown, standing 407 feet tall
summary: The fully stacked vehicle generates 18.1 million pounds-force of liftoff thrust. It's designed to transport huge payloads and people beyond Earth orbit, with both stages intended for reuse.
details: SpaceX's Starship, when fully stacked, stands at an impressive 407 feet, making it the tallest rocket ever flown. It surpasses the tallest known living tree, Hyperion, and is one-third taller than the Statue of Liberty. It's also the most powerful, with 18.1 million pounds-force of liftoff thrust.

The complete vehicle consists of two stages: the 236.2-foot Super Heavy booster and the 170.6-foot Starship spacecraft. This immense size and power are designed to transport massive payloads and eventually carry people and cargo beyond Earth orbit. SpaceX also intends to recover and reuse both stages.

The Super Heavy booster is powered by 33 Raptor engines, burning liquid methane and oxygen to produce its 18.1 million pounds-force of thrust. For comparison, NASA's Space Launch System generates 8.8 million to 9.4 million pounds of max thrust. Once Super Heavy separates, Starship continues with six Raptor engines, three of which are vacuum-optimized for space.

The rocket's immense power is needed to lift its substantial weight, including 3,650 metric tons of propellant in Super Heavy and an additional 1,600 metric tons in Starship. This totals 5,250 metric tons of propellant, requiring efficient engines, careful planning, and staging to overcome gravity.

Despite its capabilities, Starship will still require refueling in Earth orbit for missions like NASA's planned lunar landings. The SpaceX lunar lander consumes a significant amount of propellant just to reach orbit, necessitating in-space refueling.

The refueling strategy involves specialized vehicles: a propellant depot launched first, followed by tanker Starships delivering fuel. The lunar lander launches last, docks with the depot, and takes on propellant before proceeding to lunar orbit.

This complex process occurs before the crew launches aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft, which will then meet the prepositioned Starship lander in Earth orbit. The Starship lander will then transport two crew members to the Moon's surface and back, overcoming the technical challenge of storing extremely cold propellants in space.

topic: amazon degrades alexa aux input functionality
headline_marked: [[Amazon disables Alexa voice commands]] for AUX input on older Echo speakers
headline: Amazon disables Alexa voice commands for AUX input on older Echo speakers
summary: Amazon has removed the convenience of voice control for wired audio sources on several Echo models, including the Echo Plus (2nd gen), Echo (3rd/4th gen), and original Echo Studio.
details: Amazon has disabled Alexa voice controls for the AUX input on several older Echo speakers, including the second-generation Echo Plus, third-generation Echo, original Echo Studio, and fourth-generation Echo. This means commands like 'Alexa, play from line in' no longer function, frustrating users who relied on them for wired audio. The change impacts devices from 2018 to 2020.

Amazon confirmed the removal, stating it notified "the very small number of customers" who use these specific voice requests. However, the company did not provide a reason for disabling the feature. This move affects the convenience of switching to external audio sources.

Despite the voice command removal, the physical AUX connection itself remains functional. Users can still play audio through a cable and manage the AUX input settings via the Alexa app. This ensures the core functionality of the port is preserved.

The 3.5mm AUX jack on supported Echo speakers can serve as both an input and an output, depending on the model. It allows the speaker to play audio from external sources or route Alexa's audio to another speaker. Models like the 3rd/4th gen Echo and 2nd gen Echo Plus support both, while the original Echo Studio supports input only.

This means older hardware still has utility; for example, a classic CD changer can still send audio to an original Echo Studio via an RCA-to-3.5mm cable. Users can continue enjoying their physical media without needing a Bluetooth transmitter or replacing their player. The wired connection itself is unaffected.

To enable AUX input, users must open the Alexa app, select the speaker under Devices, and find 'AUX Audio' in its settings. From there, they can choose 'Line In' to play audio from an external source through the Echo. For models supporting both directions, 'Line Out' sends Echo's audio to a wired speaker.

It's important to note that Alexa's discontinued voice commands only managed the Echo's AUX input, not the playback functions of the connected equipment. Users will still need to use the source device's own controls to start playback or skip tracks. The convenience lost is purely in switching the Echo's input via voice.

Ultimately, there's no immediate need to replace an Echo device solely for its AUX port. However, upgrading to newer Echo models, such as the fifth-generation Dot which removed the 3.5mm connection entirely, will likely mean losing this feature. Future Echo Studio upgrades might also see this port disappear.
